NDT training in Dallas: how it works for Dallas employers and technicians

NDT training for Dallas-Fort Worth employers and technicians is delivered by Atlantis NDT live online or onsite at your own facility, under ASNT Level III oversight. Courses follow ASNT SNT-TC-1A for Level I, II and III in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET. The certificate itself is issued by your employer under its written practice, once documented classroom training, on-the-job experience, examinations and a vision test are complete.

The Metroplex is a hard place to run a traditional classroom course. A crew based in Irving, a fabrication shop in Grand Prairie, a pipeline contractor staging out of Cleburne and an aerospace supplier in Fort Worth can be separated by an hour or more of I-35E, I-30 or the LBJ Freeway. Pulling six technicians off the job for a week so they can sit in a room across town costs more in lost production than the course itself. That is why Atlantis does not run a Dallas training centre and does not pretend to. Theory is delivered live online, where every student can join from the shop office or home, and practical sessions happen at your facility, on your instruments and, wherever possible, on the same product forms and welds your technicians inspect every day.

Three kinds of people usually land on this page. The first is the career-changer: a welder, machinist, millwright or veteran leaving NAS Joint Reserve Base Fort Worth who wants to move into inspection and needs to understand how certification really works in Texas. The second is the working Level I who has the hours and wants a structured Level II course and exam preparation. The third is the employer: a Dallas inspection company, fabricator, midstream operator or manufacturer that needs a group trained, a written practice written or repaired, or an outside Level III to administer exams. Each section below is written for all three, and the FAQ at the end answers the questions we hear most often from DFW.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Dallas

Every course below is built on the ASNT SNT-TC-1A recommended practice and the body of knowledge ASNT publishes for each method. Classroom content is the same whether it is delivered online or onsite; what changes from one Dallas employer to the next is the practical content, which we map to the product forms, codes and acceptance criteria your technicians actually work to.

MethodLevelsWhat Dallas employers use it forPrerequisite
UT (Ultrasonic Testing)I, II, IIIThickness surveys on gathering lines and compressor-station piping in the Fort Worth Basin, shear-wave weld inspection for AWS D1.1 structural fabricators, lamination checks on plateLevel I: none beyond your written practice. Level II: UT Level I plus documented experience
PAUT (Phased Array UT)II, IIIGirth-weld inspection on transmission pipe where the code and owner allow it in place of RT, complex-geometry welds in heavy fabricationNormally UT Level II, as set by the employer's written practice
TOFD (Time of Flight Diffraction)II, IIIFlaw sizing on thick-section vessel and tank welds, usually paired with PAUT on pressure equipment fabricationNormally UT Level II
RT (Radiographic Testing)I, II, IIIAPI 1104 pipeline girth welds, ASME B31.3 process piping at compressor and processing facilities, castingsRadiation safety training and the Texas licensing requirements for the radiographer role; RT Level I before Level II
MT (Magnetic Particle Testing)I, II, IIIStructural steel and tower fabrication, railcar and heavy-equipment components, forgings and weld toesLevel I: none. Level II: MT Level I plus experience
PT (Liquid Penetrant Testing)I, II, IIIStainless and aluminium welds, non-ferrous castings, machined parts at DFW aerospace and defence suppliersLevel I: none. Level II: PT Level I plus experience
VT (Visual Testing)I, II, IIIWeld and fit-up inspection in fabrication shops, pipeline construction, bolted joints and bridge steelLevel I: none; usually the first method a new technician is certified in
ET (Eddy Current Testing)I, II, IIIFastener-hole and surface-crack inspection at aircraft maintenance operations, heat-exchanger tube inspection at power plantsLevel I: none. Level II: ET Level I plus experience

Ultrasonic Testing. The UT course starts with sound-wave physics, velocity, attenuation and the practical meaning of near field and beam spread, then moves into calibration on standard reference blocks, straight-beam thickness work and angle-beam weld inspection. For Dallas students we lean heavily on two real-world applications: corrosion and thickness mapping on midstream piping, and weld inspection on structural steel, where AWS D1.1 is the most common acceptance standard in the region's fabrication shops and data-centre steel packages. Level II students learn to write and follow a technique sheet, evaluate indications against the acceptance criteria and sign a report that will stand up to a customer audit.

Phased Array and TOFD. These are advanced ultrasonic methods and we treat them that way. Students should already hold UT Level II under their employer's written practice. The PAUT course covers focal laws, sectorial and linear scans, encoded scanning, scan plans and coverage proof; the TOFD course covers diffracted-signal theory, probe-centre-spacing selection, dead zones and through-wall sizing. In the Metroplex the demand comes mostly from pipeline construction and from heavy fabricators building pressure equipment and structural components for the energy sector.

Radiographic Testing. RT training covers radiation physics, source and X-ray tube selection, geometric unsharpness, image quality indicators, film and digital technique, and interpretation of weld and casting images. It is not a radiation licence. In Texas, industrial radiography is licensed by the state, and radiographers must also meet state training and certification requirements that are separate from their SNT-TC-1A certificate. We explain that split clearly in the course so nobody leaves thinking a Level II card lets them handle a source.

Magnetic Particle and Liquid Penetrant. These are the workhorse surface methods for DFW fabrication and manufacturing. MT covers magnetisation techniques, yokes, prods, coils and bench units, continuous versus residual methods, wet and dry particles, and field indicators. PT covers penetrant types and sensitivity levels, removal methods, dwell times and the temperature limits that matter on a Texas summer afternoon when steel sitting in the yard is far hotter than the air. Both courses finish with interpretation practice on cracked, porous and lapped samples.

Visual Testing. VT is often dismissed as easy; auditors do not see it that way. The course covers direct and remote visual technique, lighting and access, weld gauges, workmanship standards, and how to document a visual examination properly. It is the natural first certification for welders moving into inspection.

Eddy Current Testing. ET covers electromagnetic induction, impedance-plane display, probe types, frequency selection and standards. Dallas-area demand is split between aviation maintenance, where surface and near-surface crack detection around fasteners is routine, and power generation, where tube inspection in heat exchangers and condensers is outage work.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Dallas, step by step

SNT-TC-1A is a recommended practice, not a licence. In Texas, as everywhere in the United States, certification to it is employer-based. The path looks like this:

  1. Your employer adopts a written practice. This document sets out, method by method and level by level, the training hours, experience hours, examination content, passing scores, vision requirements and recertification interval that apply to its technicians. Everything else hangs off it.
  2. You complete formal classroom training. The minimum hours for each method and level are set in the written practice, which normally follows the SNT-TC-1A tables. Our training requirements matrix lists them method by method so you can plan your schedule without guessing.
  3. You build documented on-the-job experience. Experience has to be logged in the method, under supervision, and it accumulates in parallel with or after classroom training. This is almost always the longest step, especially for UT and RT at Level II.
  4. You sit the general examination. Written questions on the principles and theory of the method.
  5. You sit the specific examination. Questions on the equipment, procedures, codes and acceptance criteria your employer actually uses; in Dallas that might mean API 1104 for a pipeline contractor or AWS D1.1 for a structural fabricator.
  6. You pass the practical examination. Hands-on testing of real specimens containing known discontinuities, graded against a checklist. The general, specific and practical exams are administered or overseen by an NDT Level III designated in the written practice.
  7. You pass the vision examination. Near-vision acuity and colour-contrast differentiation, repeated annually.
  8. Your employer certifies you. The Level III and employer sign the certification record. It is valid for that employer; if you change companies, the new employer must review your records and certify you under its own written practice.
  9. You recertify on schedule. The written practice sets the interval and whether recertification is by examination or by evidence of continuing satisfactory performance.

For a fuller explanation of how the recommended practice works, see our SNT-TC-1A training and certification guide.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Dallas crews

Atlantis delivers three formats, and we will tell you honestly which one suits your situation.

  • Live online classroom. Real instructor, real-time questions, scheduled sessions. This covers the classroom-hour portion of a method and suits individual technicians and small DFW companies that cannot release a whole crew at once. See online NDT training for how sessions run.
  • Onsite at your facility. An ASNT Level III-led course delivered in your shop, yard or plant, using your equipment and specimens. This is the most efficient format for a group of four or more and the only format where practical training and practical exams are done on the exact instruments your crew uses.
  • Blended. Theory online over several weeks in short sessions that fit around production, then a compressed onsite block for practical work and exams.

Scheduling in Dallas has its own rhythm. Many Metroplex inspection companies send crews south to Gulf Coast refinery turnarounds in spring and autumn, and pipeline contractors run hardest when construction season and weather cooperate. We plan onsite blocks around those windows rather than into them, and we can split a course so part of a crew trains while the rest stays billable. Tell us your constraints and you will receive a cohort or onsite quote within one business day. Ask about onsite training for your Dallas crew, or browse the full corporate NDT training programme.

Where NDT technicians work in Dallas

Dallas-Fort Worth has no refinery row like the Houston Ship Channel, but it has a remarkably broad NDT economy. Understanding which part of it you are aiming at changes which methods to learn first.

Midstream and pipelines. Several of the largest US pipeline and gas-distribution companies are headquartered in Dallas, and the Fort Worth Basin and Barnett Shale leave a dense network of gathering lines, compressor stations and processing plants west and north of the city. Interstate lines are regulated by PHMSA under 49 CFR Parts 192 and 195; intrastate lines by the Railroad Commission of Texas pipeline safety programme. Welding and weld inspection on these lines is normally done to API 1104, which is why RT and, increasingly, automated UT and PAUT are the methods pipeline contractors ask for.

Aerospace and defence. Fort Worth is home to major military aircraft and rotorcraft manufacturing, and DFW carries heavy airline activity, with major airline headquarters at both DFW and Love Field. Aerospace NDT is normally qualified under NAS 410 rather than SNT-TC-1A, with the employer's Responsible Level III in charge. An SNT-TC-1A course from us builds method knowledge and helps technicians prepare, but it does not replace an aerospace employer's own NAS 410 qualification. We do not offer NAS 410 certification.

Power generation. Texas generation companies headquartered in the Metroplex operate gas-fired fleets across the state, and the Comanche Peak nuclear plant sits near Glen Rose, southwest of Fort Worth. Outage work pulls in UT, ET and VT technicians; nuclear owners apply ASME Section XI and their own qualification programmes on top of SNT-TC-1A, so check the owner's specific requirements before assuming a general certificate is enough.

Fabrication and manufacturing. Railcar builders, wind-tower and structural fabricators, pressure-vessel shops and the steel packages behind the region's data-centre and warehouse construction boom all rely on VT, MT and UT to AWS D1.1 and ASME Section VIII. These are some of the best entry points for new technicians in DFW because the work is steady and year-round.

Bridges and infrastructure. TxDOT's Dallas and Fort Worth districts manage a huge highway and bridge inventory, and bridge steel fabrication and field welding call for VT, MT and UT under AWS bridge welding requirements.

Industrial radiography in Texas. Texas is an NRC Agreement State. Radioactive-material licences and X-ray registrations for industrial radiography are handled by the Texas Department of State Health Services radiation control programme, and the state's industrial radiography rules (25 TAC §289.255) set out licensee duties, radiographer and trainee requirements, and radiation safety officer responsibilities. Your SNT-TC-1A RT certificate proves NDT competence; the state requirements govern who may operate sources and equipment. Employers need both.

What do Dallas employers actually ask for? In job postings and bid packages, the recurring requirements are SNT-TC-1A Level II in the specific method, experience with the code on the job (API 1104, AWS D1.1, ASME), a clean driving record for field work, and, for RT, the Texas radiographer credential. Some owners also ask for API inspector or AWS CWI credentials for supervisory roles. Atlantis does not train for API or CWI, but SNT-TC-1A certification in the core methods is the foundation that those roles sit on. For pay context, read our NDT salary guide.

Level III services and written practices for Dallas NDT companies

A large share of the NDT companies in DFW are small: a founder who holds Level II or Level III, a handful of field technicians and a growing book of customers. The first serious customer audit is often the moment they discover their written practice is a download from somewhere else, does not match the methods they actually perform, or names a Level III who left years ago. At that point every certification signed under it is open to question.

Atlantis supports Dallas employers with:

  • Written practice development and review, aligned to the current edition of SNT-TC-1A and to the methods, levels and customers you actually serve.
  • Outside Level III services: exam administration, practical specimen selection, procedure and technique review, and sign-off of certification records.
  • Recertification calendars and record audits so vision tests, expirations and experience logs never lapse unnoticed.
  • Level III preparation for your own senior technicians through our ASNT Level III training.

Book a Level III consultation and we will review your current written practice and records and tell you plainly what is missing.

Practise before the practical exam

Most people who fail a practical do so on technique, not theory: a poorly set angle-beam calibration, a missed scanning pattern, a dwell time that was too short. Our Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees practise 12 methods across five environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. For Dallas students it is a useful way to rehearse scanning and interpretation between online sessions without tying up shop equipment. It is a practice tool only. It does not replace hands-on training or the practical examination, which must be done on real specimens with real instruments.

Your instructor

Courses are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He oversees course content, written practice work and examination administration for Atlantis training programmes, and teaches across the SNT-TC-1A methods listed on this page.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Dallas

How do I get NDT certified in Dallas?

You need an employer written practice, the required classroom training, documented on-the-job experience, passing general, specific and practical exams administered by a Level III, and a current vision test. Your employer then certifies you. If you are not yet employed in NDT, start with classroom training in VT, PT or MT and apply to Dallas fabrication shops and inspection companies that will log your experience.

Can I take NDT training online in Texas?

Yes, for the classroom portion. Live online sessions count toward classroom hours when your employer's written practice accepts them, which most do. Practical training and the practical exam must be done hands-on, which is why we pair online theory with onsite sessions at your facility.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

The classroom portion can be completed in weeks; the experience requirement takes much longer. SNT-TC-1A sets separate minimums for classroom hours and for on-the-job experience, and UT Level II carries one of the larger experience requirements. Check the exact figures on our training requirements matrix and your employer's written practice.

Do I need a license for radiography in Texas?

The company needs a Texas industrial radiography licence or registration, and individual radiographers and trainees must meet the state's industrial radiography training and certification requirements. An SNT-TC-1A RT certificate alone does not authorise you to operate a source or X-ray unit.

What does NDT training cost in Dallas?

It depends on the method, level, group size and whether you choose online, onsite or blended delivery. We do not publish prices; cohort and onsite quotes are returned within one business day. Request a Dallas training quote.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Dallas employers?

SNT-TC-1A is the most widely used qualification framework in North American industrial NDT, and Dallas pipeline, fabrication and power employers work to it. Aerospace employers generally use NAS 410 instead, and certain owners add their own requirements.

Do you have a training centre in Dallas?

No. Atlantis delivers training live online and onsite at employers' facilities across DFW. That keeps crews close to work and lets practical training happen on the equipment they use.

Which NDT method should I learn first?

For most new technicians in Dallas, VT then PT or MT, followed by UT. These methods have the shortest paths to certification and are in constant demand in fabrication shops, which gives you the experience base for UT and RT.

Will my certification transfer if I change employers?

Not automatically. SNT-TC-1A certification belongs to the employer. Your training and experience records do travel with you, and a new employer can review them and certify you under its own written practice, usually after its own exams.

Can you train my crew at our shop in Fort Worth or Arlington?

Yes. Onsite training anywhere in the Metroplex is a standard format. We plan around your production and send a quote within one business day.

Do you offer API or CWI training?

No. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A only. Some Dallas employers ask for API or AWS CWI credentials for inspection supervisors, and our SNT-TC-1A courses build the method knowledge those roles rely on.

Can you help us pass a customer audit of our NDT programme?

Yes. Our Level III reviews your written practice, certification records, exam files and vision records, then fixes gaps before the auditor finds them.
